items.excerpt: Figma's Sightlines newsletter no.2 gathers senior design and product leaders on what it takes to design agentic products. The core problem: agents are powerful, but interfaces must earn trust and make permissions and security legible to users.

IRONMACE's non-technical president used the AI coding assistant Aura to build Dark and Darker's tutorial system directly against the game codebase in about two weeks — work the team estimated at five to six weeks. A concrete case of a non-engineer shipping production features.

Artist Blue Nile deliberately under-trains 3D Gaussian Splats and films from a moving bus, then composites in Blender, turning a reconstruction 'failure mode' into a dreamlike aesthetic. A craft argument for using neural capture artifacts on purpose.

Top-down 'use AI' mandates raise output expectations without delivering real productivity, because time saved on generation is eaten by verification and coordination. Builder argues AI only pays off when wired into the systems where design and dev teams actually collaborate.

Four Fish Audio text-to-speech and transcription models are now on Vercel AI Gateway, free for 30 days. Voice generation becomes a one-line dependency for prototypes, putting audio UI inside the same workflow as generative interface builds.

A practical breakdown of which design system documentation should be generated automatically from code and tokens, and which parts — intent, rationale, usage judgement — must stay human-authored. Automating the wrong layer produces docs nobody trusts.

A handoff checklist arguing the design system is infrastructure, not an artifact: tokens, component contracts, state docs, responsive specs. It cites design-system-aware AI cutting UI delivery time 46.7–69.4%, and warns that codegen without a documented system just accelerates inconsistency.

A working mobile UX designer's account of where AI actually lands in the process: it collapses the endless wireframe iteration loop, not the judgement work. The remaining job is empathy, strategy and framing the real human problem.

Most shipped AI features are bolt-on chat panels that add steps instead of removing them. The argument: good AI design is invisible — it absorbs tedious work inside existing flows rather than announcing itself as a new surface.

August's AI dev tool rankings mark the largest single-month shake-up yet: Claude Opus 5 debuts at the top with a 1691 Elo, and Kimi K3 becomes the first open-weight model in the top three. Four new entrants reset which model teams should default to for build work.

Deloitte research finds the hard part of agentic AI isn't the technology but organizational readiness: nearly two-thirds of executives are rethinking business models around agents, yet fewer than half feel prepared operationally. Piloting agents without process redesign stalls at the pilot.
